project.name: Representative Hardware Project
project.objective: Deliver a verified hardware-connected software capability.
definition_of_done: Approved architecture is decomposed into independently verifiable work.
constraints: Physical hardware claims require representative evidence

architecture.summary: Separate protocol, transport, device abstraction, application logic and validation boundaries.
boundaries: Workers may not change public interfaces without architecture approval

risks: Simulation may diverge from physical hardware

routing.policy: Assign the cheapest capability tier expected to satisfy objective acceptance criteria.

domain.baseline: Fictional serial test adapter repository at its synthetic known-good tag; no physical device. Source: synthetic fixture specification.
domain.hardware_identity: Fictional SYNTH-SENSOR-1 board revision A, firmware 0.0.0-synthetic; establishes no real hardware behavior.
domain.interfaces: Line-based loopback interface, SYNTH-FRAME-1 synthetic wire format, version 1.
domain.specifications: The synthetic fixture specification embedded in examples/software-hardware; no manufacturer document exists.
domain.environment: Python 3.12 host tests only; no deployment target.
domain.known_paths: Known-good: fake device round trip in the sample tests. Known-failing: none observed, because no hardware has been observed.
domain.validation_resources: Local fake device and loopback transport only; physical hardware claims remain unverified.
domain.physical_access: No physical unit exists; hardware-in-loop checks in the sample can only be attested by an operator who has one.
domain.architecture_boundaries: Frame format, transport contract and the device abstraction boundary require user approval to change.

workflow.policy: One bounded issue per task; link validation and independent review in a PR; accept only inside the approved foundation.
